name: PA-14
label: Safe R

key_factors: Reschenthaler's large fundraising and cash advantage
No polling or expert ratings; markets price Democrat at ~2%
model.rationale: The R+17 lean, Reschenthaler's incumbency and roughly ten-to-one fundraising edge over Bradstock leave little evidence of a competitive race, and prediction markets price the Democrat at about 2%. The forecast stays near the fundamentals-based margin with no polls to justify a bigger move.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing the incumbent under 55% or a surge of Democratic outside spending would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Guy Reschenthaler seeks another term in a southwestern Pennsylvania district that leans heavily Republican, with a partisan edge of about 17 points toward the GOP. He is a well-funded incumbent, having raised over $4 million and holding nearly $1 million on hand, while Democrat Alan Bradstock has raised about $370,000 with modest cash reserves. Neither side has drawn meaningful outside spending.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money. Prediction markets give the Democrat roughly a 2% chance of winning. The seat is rated safely Republican, with the incumbent favored by a wide but not insurmountable margin given the absence of direct polling.
